text:
In my opinion, the belief that manufactured homes inherently depreciate while site-built homes appreciate is an oversimplification. What tends to appreciate is desirable real estate in desirable locations. The structure itself, whether manufactured or site-built, is only one component of a property's overall value. When manufactured homes are located in attractive, supply-constrained markets and are properly maintained, their values can and do respond to the same market forces that affect other residential properties.

The value of a property includes both the land and the improvements on it. New manufactured homes cost much less than site-built homes, largely because the cost of the land and the necessary utility preparation are not included.

The next element in valuation is the land itself. Most manufactured homes are located either in more affordable rural communities on privately owned land or within mobile home communities where the lot is leased from a park owner or owned collectively by residents through a cooperative (co-op) arrangement. These factors often contribute to lower manufactured home values when compared with site-built homes.

However, that is not depreciation in the same way a car depreciates. Manufactured homes, regardless of the ownership scenario, have values that are tied to the real estate market. During COVID, we lived in a lot-lease community in Florida where most existing homes dated from 1984 through the early 1990s, with a sprinkling of models from 2017 to 2020. In the years immediately before COVID, well-maintained and reasonably updated homes in our neighborhood typically sold for $45 to $60 per square foot. As the Florida real estate market went crazy and homes began receiving multiple offers, manufactured home prices in lot lease communities increased to $60 to $100 per square foot and were selling very quickly.

We bought our home in that lot-lease community in 2017 for $12,000. It was the lowest-priced home in the neighborhood because the seller was highly motivated to sell. The home had been well maintained, with a newer metal roof, HVAC system, and water heater. The previous owner had also installed new laminate flooring throughout, but the rest of the interior was essentially original. At the time, similarly maintained homes were selling for around $20,000, while more updated homes were selling for $40,000 to $60,000.

We had planned to update the décor, but we soon realized that Florida was not going to be our permanent home. Every time we considered spending money on cosmetic improvements, we agreed that we would rather save that money for our eventual move back to Texas.

The home we purchased in Texas was also among the lower-priced properties in its rural market. Many homes of similar size, around 1,600 square feet, are listed in the $200,000s and higher, although property sizes and locations can vary significantly.

In real estate, "location, location, location" remains the most important factor in determining value. If major metropolitan areas allowed manufactured homes in mixed neighborhoods alongside site-built homes, and those homes were well maintained, offered comparable finishes and amenities, and were attractively situated on their lots rather than simply placed with minimal site improvements, their values would likely track much more closely with neighboring site-built homes over time.

For that reason, I believe it is more accurate to say that manufactured homes are often located in markets that place limits on their value, rather than to say they automatically depreciate because they are manufactured homes. As with any other type of housing, condition, location, land ownership, local demand, and the overall real estate market ultimately play the largest roles in determining long-term value.

text:
Two little towns in Todd County, Kentucky, put together a new government board and it was given $30 million in funding and power to take land for a 53-mile natural gas pipeline. 

The two towns are Guthrie and Trenton, Kentucky. Combined have fewer than 2,000 people. Most of the farms this pipe is running across aren’t even in the same county, let alone the same towns.

They’re offering about $5,800 an acre for the strip they want to build on. Land in the area is selling for around $10,000 - $20,000 an acre. They want another 30-foot temporary construction easement on top of that, at an even lower rate. So not only are they offering below-market rates for the land, but they’re also causing permanent damage to the farmland they aren’t purchasing. Not to mention the impact on property values.

If you refuse the lowball offer, they file for condemnation and take it anyway through eminent domain, using millions in taxpayer funds to drag you through court.

State taxpayers have sent them $30 million so far. They’ve burned through $7–8 million already, according to recent statements from the board’s head, and they haven’t even built a thing yet. The whole project is expected to cost $120–$150 million. The worst part about the spending is that they haven’t set up any real public accounting of where the money is going.

They say they’re building it for economic development, so the new agency can own the pipe and sell capacity mostly to the two towns that created it, in addition to Fort Campbell and Clarksville. The people whose land is getting cut up and subjected to a permanent easement—and whose property values could decline—will most likely never see a bit of the gas going through the pipeline.

The Public Service Commission has already said a project like this is unprecedented for a municipal outfit. The government created the board, funded it with tax money, gave it eminent domain authority, and is using it to seize private property so it can generate its own revenue.

Who does this serve, and why? Is this the government serving the people it’s supposed to? Or does the government just want to create more revenue for the sake of generating more revenue? Are the people in these areas of Kentucky clamoring for a new gas pipeline so Clarksville, Tennessee, can benefit?

Were they asked whether the cost of this “economic development” would be worth it? Or did a bunch of government officials get in a room and rub their hands together while thinking about all those sweet, sweet dollar bills they’ll get from “new revenue” sources, promising themselves they’ll really use the money to help their constituents… this time… they promise.

text:
Vietnam and Algocracy

As digital transformation accelerates, Vietnam is transitioning into a highly digitalized state, increasingly relying on artificial intelligence (AI) and automated decision-making (ADM) systems to administer public services, manage resources, and maintain internal security. This paradigm shift gives rise to "algocracy"—a system in which algorithms are utilized to collect, collate, and organize the data upon which critical governance decisions are made.1 While proponents champion algocracy for its promise of frictionless administration and hyper-efficiency, its rapid integration into the Vietnamese public sector has precipitated profound shifts in state-citizen dynamics.
In the specific context of Vietnam's single-party state, rapid digital transformation is actively leveraged to consolidate authority, creating an architecture that researchers have termed "Panopticon 2.0".3 This report provides an analysis of how algorithmic governance is applied in Vietnam. By examining the theoretical underpinnings of algorithmic power, the dynamics of AI adoption in local government, the coercive enforcement of biometric infrastructures like the VNeID system, and the country's sweeping new 2026 AI legislation, this analysis illuminates how digital modernization is utilized to tighten state control over biopower and mandate systemic compliance.

The Theoretical Framework of Algorithmic Power in an Autocratic Context
Algocracy, Biopower, and State Discipline
The concept of algocracy describes a systemic shift wherein the state's reliance on computer programs to execute public functions fundamentally alters the relationship between the government and the governed. In democratic contexts, the primary threat posed by algocracy is the erosion of republican liberty and contestability—when citizens cannot understand or challenge opaque algorithmic decisions, they are subjected to arbitrary power.1
However, in an autocratic context like Vietnam, the deployment of algorithmic infrastructure does not merely suffer from an accidental "trust deficit"; rather, it is designed to bypass the need for public trust through absolute, automated compliance. The Vietnamese state utilizes digital transformation to tighten its grip on biopower, disciplining the population into accepting a state-led surveillance society that is framed around narratives of "convenience," "efficiency," and "modernity".3
The Trias Algorithmica and Centralized Control
The concentration of algorithmic power typically requires a robust constitutional response, such as the Trias Algorithmica—the structural separation of the entities that design algorithmic rules from those that execute and audit them.5 In Vietnam, however, this separation of powers is actively resisted. The state intentionally fuses legislative, executive, and judicial-like algorithmic functions under centralized control, allowing the political apparatus to embed its objective functions directly into the digital infrastructure deployed across the nation.3

The Realities of Algorithmic Bureaucracy in Local Government
While the central authorities push a highly sophisticated digital vision, the actual adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) in Vietnamese local government reveals significant organizational friction.
Local civil servants face an "AI accountability vacuum"—a state of governance paralysis where GenAI use is simultaneously encouraged by high-level digital transformation mandates but discouraged by a lack of legal and regulatory frameworks.10 A reconstructive look at Vietnamese local administration reveals several critical failure modes in AI adoption12:

- Absence of Implementation Plans:General directives from provincial leaders are issued without specific strategies, workflows, or usage guidelines, leaving employees without direction.
- Insufficient Funding:No dedicated budgets exist for purchasing secure GenAI subscriptions. 
- Fear of Security Risks:Civil servants fear inputting sensitive state data into unvetted, general-purpose GenAI tools, severely limiting the integration of AI into official workflows.
- Regulatory Void:Because AI outputs are probabilistic rather than rule-based, employees fear career repercussions for unauthorized or improperly governed technology use in a compliance-heavy bureaucracy.

Consequently, GenAI adoption at the local level remains informal, voluntary, and highly fragmented, driven by individual experimentation rather than institutional transformation.

Infrastructural Control, Biometric Enforcement, and Censorship
At the national level, the Vietnamese state demonstrates immense capability in utilizing digital infrastructure as a tool of absolute control. The cornerstone of this architecture is the VNeID system, a mandatory national digital identity platform that requires citizens and residents to submit extensive personal, medical, and biometric information.13
Biometric Financial Enforcement
The coercive power of the VNeID infrastructure was vividly demonstrated when, beginning in September 2025, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) enforced a mandate affecting approximately 86 million bank accounts.13 Individuals who had not completed in-person facial biometric authentication with their banks were instantly denied access to their funds, with their accounts frozen or closed without a grace period. This mandate, particularly applied to large transfers, illustrates how biometric enforcement allows the state to instantly revoke basic economic participation for non-compliance. The state's ability to safely manage this vast repository of sensitive data is heavily contested, particularly following incidents like the CIC data breach, which highlighted severe security vulnerabilities.14
Digital Integration with the Political Apparatus
The VNeID system is designed to deeply integrate the population with the ruling Communist Party's apparatus. Upcoming features for the application include voter engagement modules, draft document feedback portals, and direct integration with the Party's internal communications systems in preparation for the National Party Congress.13
Furthermore, the state continuously pressures transnational platforms to comply with its censorship regime. This was solidified by a 2026 memorandum signed between Meta and Vietnam's Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism, designed to systematically tighten online censorship and suppress digital dissent on platforms like Facebook and Threads.15

The Legal Governance of AI in Vietnam
To legitimize its digital infrastructure and regulate the rapidly expanding tech sector, Vietnam has enacted sophisticated, sweeping legislation.
The 2026 AI Law
Taking effect on March 1, 2026, Vietnam's new Law on Artificial Intelligence introduces a European-style, risk-based governance framework.11 
The law also mandates that AI-generated audio, image, and video content must be clearly labeled to prohibit the use of AI for activities that threaten national security or public order. 
The Law on Digital Technology Industry
Complementing the AI Law is the Law on Digital Technology Industry, passed by the National Assembly and effective January 1, 2026.17 This law establishes a comprehensive legal regime for digital and coded assets (including cryptocurrencies) and offers substantial tax relief and public funding incentives for R&D in AI, blockchain, and semiconductor technologies.
However, beneath this pro-innovation regulatory veneer, the legal architecture firmly centralizes the national AI ecosystem under state control. The infrastructure is designed to serve as a unified, state-directed mechanism that, when combined with cybersecurity laws, deeply entrenches the state's capacity for surveillance and transnational repression.3

Conclusion
The rapid expansion of algocracy in Vietnam represents a highly coordinated effort to fuse technological modernization with single-party political control. While the state has constructed a legal architecture—highlighted by the 2026 AI Law and the Law on Digital Technology Industry—these frameworks are deployed not to foster democratic accountability, but to formalize a risk-based approach to state security and digital sovereignty.
Through the mandatory implementation of the VNeID biometric system and the unprecedented financial freezing of 86 million unverified bank accounts, the Vietnamese state has demonstrated that algorithmic infrastructure can be weaponized to guarantee absolute societal compliance. Simultaneously, the struggle of local bureaucracies to implement GenAI amidst funding shortages and an "accountability vacuum" reveals the practical limits of top-down digital mandates. Ultimately, Vietnam's trajectory serves as a definitive case study in digital authoritarianism, illustrating how AI and digital governance are engineered to bypass public trust and establish a permanent, high-tech surveillance state.

text:
Everyone is building AI products for other AI builders.

Meanwhile, a roofer is paying $228 per lead just to get someone to look at a leaking roof.

That’s the opportunity most people are ignoring.

There are 36.2 million small businesses in the US. Most don't need another AI tool. They need more customers, more booked jobs, and more money in the bank.

Here’s the AI business I’d start right now:

Build an AI-powered marketing agency for boring, high-ticket local businesses.

Think roofing companies, septic services, foundation repair, garage floor coatings, commercial refrigeration, dental implants, and waterproofing.

Why these businesses?

→ Their services can be worth thousands of dollars.
→ Customers already have urgent problems and are ready to buy.
→ Many have weak websites, confusing offers, and poor follow-up systems.
→ One additional customer can generate enough revenue to justify your entire service fee.
And here's the key:
Don't sell AI. Sell the outcome.
Don't tell a roofer you're building an AI automation system.

Tell them you're helping turn more website visitors into booked roof inspections.

Don't sell a chatbot.

Sell a system that responds to missed calls in under a minute.

Don't sell another website.

Build a conversion funnel that helps turn existing traffic into paying customers.

The business owner doesn't care about your tech stack. They care about whether the phone rings.

Here's how to build the business:

1. Pick one niche.

Don't chase every industry at once.

Look for businesses with high-ticket services, urgent customer demand, weak online competition, and owners you can contact directly.

Go one level deeper than the obvious niches.

Everyone targets plumbers and HVAC companies. Explore garage floor coatings, landscape lighting, sauna installations, chimney services, septic companies, and commercial hood cleaning.

Less competition can mean more room to stand out.

2. Find the gaps in their marketing.

Use AI agents to research 100 businesses in one city.

Audit their websites and ask:

• How quickly can a visitor find the phone number?
• Is there a compelling offer?
• Can customers request a quote or book an inspection easily?
• Does the business capture leads before visitors leave?
• What happens after someone submits a form?
• Are missed calls and estimates followed up properly?

Rank businesses by their biggest conversion problems.

You're not necessarily looking for businesses without traffic.

You're looking for businesses wasting the traffic they already have.
3. Build a funnel, not just a website.
A good funnel might include:
→ A landing page with a clear offer.
→ A quick assessment or quote request.
→ A simple booking process.
→ Automated SMS and email follow-ups.
→ Appointment reminders.
→ Follow-up sequences for people who haven't booked.
→ Tracking to measure leads, appointments, and sales.
For example, a roofing company could offer a free roof assessment, let homeowners answer a few questions, and make booking an inspection effortless.
AI coding agents can help build the pages, write the copy, generate creative assets, and implement much of the follow-up logic.

You'll still need to verify the work, connect the client's systems, and make sure the entire process actually functions.

4. Make the offer impossible to misunderstand.

Compare these two pitches:

❌ "I provide AI-powered marketing automation and conversion optimization."

✅ "I'll help you turn more of your existing website visitors into booked inspections without automatically increasing your ad spend."

The second pitch speaks directly to the business owner's problem.
Use simple language. Focus on customer pain points, speed, trust, and the next action the customer needs to take.
5. Use AI to deliver faster.
What once required a strategist, copywriter, designer, and developer can now be produced much faster with the right AI tools and workflow.
Research the market. Analyze competing offers. Build the funnel. Write the follow-up sequences. Generate the assets. Test the experience.
But remember: AI can accelerate production. It cannot guarantee conversions or replace understanding the customer.
6. Charge for business value, not hours.

The model outlined in the original breakdown looks like this:

• $2,500–$5,000 for a funnel installation.
• $1,500/month for ongoing optimization and support.

Five clients paying $1,500/month would generate $7,500 in monthly recurring revenue, before expenses.

Those are example price points, not guaranteed market rates. Your pricing should depend on the client's economics, the scope of work, and your ability to deliver measurable value.

7. Get your first client with a personalized audit.

You don't need a huge portfolio to start.

Pick one business. Audit its website. Identify three specific problems. Build a sample landing page or funnel in its branding.

Then send the owner a short, personalized message explaining what you found.

For example:

"I noticed customers have to go through several steps to request an inspection on your website. I mocked up a simpler booking experience that could make it easier for homeowners to contact you. Would you be open to a 15-minute walkthrough?"

Show them the solution instead of sending another generic agency pitch.

Start with one client, learn the industry, document the results, and turn the experience into a case study.

Then repeat the process.

The biggest lesson:

You don't need to invent the next billion-dollar AI startup to build a profitable AI business.

You can use existing AI tools to solve an expensive, boring, everyday problem for a business that already has customers and revenue.
Start with one niche.

Find one painful problem.

Build one solution.

Get one case study.

Then scale what works.

Everyone is fighting for attention in the AI bubble.

There's a whole market of traditional businesses that simply want more customers.

The opportunity isn't just building AI. It's using AI to deliver results that businesses already pay for.

text:
One of the best op-ed pieces worth reading.

Coca Camhi wrote:

Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything, and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations so that I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbour that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbours. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honour, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit.

text:
CharacterAI has voluntarily filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in federal court in Delaware, signaling a dramatic shift for one of the most prominent consumer chatbot platforms born out of the initial generative artificial intelligence boom. The startup entered court-supervised restructuring after facing unsustainable operational costs and an escalating wave of severe legal challenges, including high-profile personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits alleging that its conversational models encouraged self-harm and mental health crises among teenage users. Along with statutory litigation from multiple state attorneys general, these mounting liabilities choked off capital investment, rendering the platform's standalone business model financially unviable.

As part of the restructuring process, CharacterAI secured a twenty million dollar asset purchase agreement with The Walt Disney Company, designating the media conglomerate as the stalking-horse bidder in a court-sanctioned auction. Under the proposed transaction, Disney will acquire a non-exclusive, perpetual license to specific proprietary technology, software assets, and intellectual property developed by the startup. This agreement comes shortly after Disney appointed former CharacterAI executive leadership to oversee its broader technology strategy, positioning the entertainment giant to selectively integrate conversational modeling frameworks into its digital offerings while leaving CharacterAI’s legal liabilities behind in bankruptcy court.

Despite entering Chapter 11 proceedings, CharacterAI plans to keep its consumer-facing website and mobile application operational in the short term. The company has filed customary first-day motions requesting judicial authorization to maintain day-to-day operations, pay employee wages, and compensate critical infrastructure vendors while navigating the court-monitored sales process. Management intends to use the bankruptcy grace period to run a competitive bidding process, allowing higher or better offers to emerge for the company's remaining assets and operating platform before final approvals are executed.

However, the startup explicitly acknowledged that if no qualified buyer emerges willing to acquire and fund the underlying consumer business as a going concern, the CharacterAI platform will ultimately be wound down and permanently shut down following the court sale. The bankruptcy filing highlights the increasing financial, legal, and ethical hurdles confronting consumer AI startups operating outside the protective ecosystem of major technology conglomerates. By leveraging Chapter 11, CharacterAI attempts an orderly liquidation of its technology assets, providing a stark example of how regulatory scrutiny and liability risks are accelerating consolidation across the generative artificial intelligence industry.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars
The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

10 PM Top-of-the-Hour News

Prayers are pouring in from around the world for Pope Leo, who was diagnosed with lung cancer today, after a 3 hour lung nodule operation. Brad Gibson reports: “It now appears that in preoperative tests that doctors suspected Pope Leo had cancer. The Vatican did not say whether the Pope would undergo further treatment, but the information released seems to indicate he has early stage lung cancer, which is typically treated with surgery and tends to have a very high survival rate. ”
The pontiff is now resting comfortably.

Speaking at a rally in Alaska today, President Trump urged supporters to re-elect Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and warned of the consequences of a Democratic victory in the upcoming midterms.: “I've done more for this state than any other state in the union, and they'll repeal it immediately. ”
Trump was joined at the rally by Sullivan and Congressman Nick Begich, who's also running for reelection.

Sparks are flying in Georgia tonight – at the latest debate between Democrat incumbent Jon Ossoff and Republican Congressman Mike Collins. Ossoff leaned into Collins repeatedly asking him why he supported the war in Iran: “It's been months and months. 21 Americans have been killed, hundreds wounded. It's never cost more to fill up your truck. We have a global energy crisis, and Congressman Collins to this day continues to defend the war. I think that Georgians deserve to know, Congressman, how this war has helped them. Iran still has its uranium, its drones, its missiles. How has this war helped Georgians? ”
Collins responded that he found the question ironic – since Ossoff is backing Michigan Democratic hopeful Abdul El-Sayed who has voiced his opposition to the war and his opposition to Israel.

Duane Davis has been sentenced in a Las Vegas courtroom to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the drive-by shooting death of Tupac Shakur. The rapper's sister, Sekyiwa Shakur offered a victim impact statement...: “I miss my brother. I do, I do, I do. I miss his skin. I miss his scars on his head. ”
Shakur died in 1996 near the Las Vegas strip.

A fatal accident at an Georgia Six Flags amusement park has prompted the temporary closure of nine rides at six other parks across the country. One man died and four other riders were injured.
NewsNation's Marni Hughes reports...: “Authorities and park officials have yet to say what caused this, but eyewitnesses say the man fell from the park's Goliath roller coaster on Monday. Six Flags released a statement saying that our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guests, family, friends, and loved ones, and we're providing support to the guests and team members affected. The company says they are also cooperating with authorities as the investigation is pending. ”
The victim has been identified as 42 year old Hassam Kareem who was a father to a 10-year-old daughter and an educator in Atlanta, Georgia.

The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is being filled with water again after another round of repairs. WWNN’s Stacy Lyn reports:: “The pool has been drained and refilled several times since President Trump launched a renovation project this summer ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary celebration, but soon after the work was first completed, algae spread across the water and parts of the new coating appeared to peel off. Former Olympic swimmer David Hearn was accused of damaging the pool, but the charges. Were later dropped, which the president was clearly not happy about. Really disappointed with Jeanine Pirro. She she folded like an umbrella, and people get away with things. It's a disgrace. Trump says the second round of renovations is now complete and water is flowing back in. Stacy Linn, Worldwide News Network, Washington. ”

text:
Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird led a coalition of 23 state attorneys general in urging the National Judicial College to sever its partnership with the Environmental Law Institute over the nonprofit's longstanding ties to China.

The National Judicial College, a prominent training institution based in Reno, Nevada, risks its credibility by working with the ELI and its Climate Judiciary Project, according to Bird's letter.

The attorneys general pointed to a $215,000 grant the college accepted in 2021 to train state judges as climate-education resources, alongside additional ELI donations in 2023 and joint webinars hosted as recently as January.

These concerns stem from a June report by the national security group State Armor, which alleged the ELI has partnered for decades with Chinese universities, judges, and regulators linked to the Chinese Communist Party, including military research and influence operations.

Bird argued that judicial impartiality is put at risk when judges receive training from an organization influenced by a hostile foreign government.

The coalition requested that the college suspend distribution of ELI materials, preserve related records, direct the ELI to stop claiming the college's endorsement, and review its curricula for improper foreign influence.

The letter does not name any specific judge or court ruling shown to have been swayed by Chinese interests.

The ELI has firmly rejected the allegations, stating its Climate Judiciary Project offers voluntary, evidence-based education and does not instruct judges on how to decide cases.

Bird was joined by Republican attorneys general from 22 other states, spanning from Alabama and Florida to Texas and Wyoming.

The request follows a parallel investigation launched by the House Judiciary Committee in January, which issued a recent staff report alleging the ELI actively sought to steer judges toward specific climate-liability outcomes.

text:
This is who built America:Ewen Cameron
In late December 1842, the Mier Expedition was a raid on the Mexican border settlement of Ciudad Mier, which turned into the Batalla de Mier when the Mexican Army arrived. Cameron and the other Texans were taken prisoner, after inflicting a large number of casualties on the other side.
At a location called El Rancho Salado, a jar containing 159 white beans and 17 black beans was presented to the Texan prisoners. Each man drew a bean from the jar, while blindfolded. The 17 Texan prisoners who drew black beans were executed at dusk by a Mexican firing squad. This is known as the Black Bean Episode and occurred on March 25, 1843, three months after the Battle of Mier.
Cameron had selected a white bean, which should have saved his life. Yet he had earned the hostility of Mexican Colonel Antonio Canales Rosillo for his role in his embarrassing defeat in the Battle at Fort of Lipantitlán, Texas, in July 1842, and for Cameron's role in leading an escape attempt. Colonel Canales urged the Mexican dictator Antonio López de Santa Anna to have Cameron executed.
On April 25, 1843, the prisoners who had drawn white beans were being moved to Mexico City. As they traveled, a courier arrived with orders from Santa Anna for Cameron's execution. Cameron was shot by a firing squad at Perote Prison in the state of Veracruz, the next morning, April 26, 1843. Cameron refused to confess to a priest, and declined the offer of a blindfold, declaring, "For the liberty of Texas, Ewen Cameron can look death in the face." He then opened his hunting shirt and yelled at his executioners, "Fuego!"

A new nasal spray reversed signs of brain aging and restored memory performance in preclinical trials — and it worked in just weeks.

Scientists at Texas A&M University have unveiled a potential game-changer in cognitive health: an experimental nasal spray that appears to reverse key markers of brain aging.

The therapy targets 'neuroinflammaging'—the chronic, low-level inflammation deep in the brain's memory center that slowly degrades cognitive function and increases the risk for conditions like Alzheimer's disease.

By delivering microscopic biological packages known as extracellular vesicles directly into the nasal passages, the treatment easily bypasses the blood-brain barrier without requiring surgical or invasive procedures.

In preclinical trials, just two doses spaced two weeks apart produced remarkable results within weeks, calming hyperactive immune cells, restoring neuronal cellular energy, and significantly boosting memory performance for several months. While human clinical trials are still needed to confirm these findings in patients, the breakthrough suggests that age-related mental decline may not be an irreversible fate after all.

Researchers hope this accessible approach could one day offer a simple, non-invasive alternative to complex neurological treatments and prolonged medications.

source: Shetty, A. K., Narayana, M. L., & Kodali, M. (2026). Reversing age-related brain inflammation and cognitive decline using intranasal extracellular vesicles. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles

I recently had the opportunity to meet @TheAKGuy, who is running for Congress in Texas, at @TXGunRights event. And I genuinely enjoyed our conversation.

One thing that stood out to me was how openly he spoke about losing his previous election. He actually said he was happy he lost. Not because he didn't care, but because, looking back, he realized he wasn't ready at the time. Now, he believes he is.

Listening to him talk about his vision for Texas, his plans for the future, and the community he hopes to represent was refreshing.

I even offered to cater one of his campaign events for free as a professional chef. He respectfully declined, explaining that accepting the offer would raise campaign-finance concerns. I appreciated that he took those rules seriously.

As a veteran, former law enforcement officer, and small-business owner, I have my own perspective on leadership, service, and the challenges everyday Americans face.

I walked away from that conversation with a great deal of respect for Brandon and a renewed sense of optimism about the future of Texas.

Regardless of politics, I believe there's something valuable about meeting candidates face-to-face, hearing their stories, and understanding what motivates them to serve.

If you have the ability to legally and fairly vote for Brandon in this upcoming election, please do so! I cannot endorse a politician enough.

Defending the Word of God against false teaching and syncretism is a biblical imperative. Jude 3 explicitly commands believers to "earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints." When public figures put forward teachings that undermine the exclusivity of the cross—whether through sentimentality that silences Romans 10 or legal systems that offer an alternate track to righteousness—leaving those claims unchallenged allows spiritual confusion to spread unchecked.

By standing firm on the written Word, the biblical standard remains absolute:

The Exclusivity of Christ: Salvation from the wrath of God is found solely through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ, who is the sole mediator between God and man (1 Timothy 2:5, Acts 4:12). Scripture establishes that no human heritage, moral framework, or legal system can justify a fallen sinner apart from the shed blood and imputed righteousness of the Lamb (Romans 3:20–26, Galatians 2:21).

The Insufficiency of Syncretic Frameworks: Post-Second Temple rabbinic codes and extrabiblical legal traditions carry no covenantal or salvific authority over the conscience of man (Mark 7:7–9, Colossians 2:8). Canonical Scripture does not present the return of Jesus Christ as the execution of rabbinic civil ordinances, but as the holy judgment of the King of kings against all ungodliness and worldly rebellion through the power of His living Word (Isaiah 11:4, Revelation 19:11–16).

The Preservation of the True Gospel: Justification before a holy God is never attained through personal moral effort, civic decency, or human legal observance (Romans 3:20, Titus 3:5). Any framework that proposes a path to righteousness or entrance into eternal life apart from the atoning work of Jesus Christ compromises the New Covenant (Galatians 1:6–9, Galatians 2:21).

The proclamation of this uncompromised Gospel remains the sole mandate of the faithful. True biblical charity does not flatter men in their self-righteousness or invent parallel covenants to court earthly approval; it points every soul—without distinction or partiality—to the cross of Jesus of Nazareth. To diminish the necessity of Christ is to leave men under divine condemnation; to proclaim Him boldly is to hold forth the only Name by which we must be saved.

text:
This explanation exposes the root error: attempting to merge the New Covenant with Talmudic two-covenant theology.   
1. A False Path to Righteousness
Quoting Maimonides to argue that Gentiles can be "righteous before God" and gain the world to come apart from Christ through seven commands guts the Gospel (Galatians 2:21). Scripture is absolute: "There is none righteous, no, not one" (Rom 3:10). Salvation and eternal life come exclusively through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ, not adherence to a rabbinic legal framework (Acts 4:12).   
2. Misappropriating Acts 15
The Jerusalem Council was not adopting a Talmudic Noahide code to offer Gentiles an alternative track to God. Acts 15 dealt with Gentiles who were already regenerated by faith in Jesus (Acts 15:7–9, 11). The pastoral instructions in verse 20 were rooted in Leviticus 17–18 to preserve table fellowship between Jewish and Gentile believers in the body of Christ, not to endorse an extrabiblical rabbinic paradigm.   
3. Christ Does Not Enforce Rabbinic Jurisprudence
Projecting Sanhedrin 57a and Maimonides' penal codes onto Revelation 19 to portray Christ as the executioner of Talmudic jurisprudence is an astonishing distortion. The sharp sword proceeding from His mouth is the living Word of God executing divine wrath upon an unbelieving world (Isa 11:4, Rev 19:15)—not a magistrate enforcing post-temple rabbinic law.   
4. The Core Issue: The Exclusivity of Christ
Under orthodox rabbinic categories, worshiping Jesus as God incarnate is fundamentally incompatible with their definition of monotheism. Where in canonical Scripture are believers commanded to point the nations to an extrabiblical Noahide framework instead of the Cross? Jesus did not commission His disciples to teach rabbinic civil codes; He commanded them to preach the Gospel to every creature (Mark 16:15). There is one mediator, one covenant of grace, and one Name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved.

Finally, the greatest tragedy of promoting an extrabiblical Noahide framework is that it comforts men in their spiritual blindness while withholding the warning of Scripture. The Apostle Paul did not mince words: those who reject the Messiah are broken off from the olive tree due to unbelief (Rom 11:20), and seeking righteousness through legal systems leaves them under the severity of God (Rom 11:22). Christ Himself declared plainly to those relying on their lineage and traditions: "If ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins" (John 8:24). True biblical love does not invent separate tracks for the nations or flatter rabbinic systems; it warns all men—Jew and Gentile alike—that apart from faith in Jesus Christ, they remain under condemnation (John 3:36; Rom 2:9). The only path to the World to Come is through the cross of Jesus of Nazareth.

WA State Office of Refugee and Immigration Assistance (ORIA)

Oct. 13, 2026

Welcoming Washington:

ORIA Newsletter - October 2026

Highlights

☆ Public Charge Rule Change

On Sept. 18, 2026, a new public charge rule went into effect. The Washington State Office of Refugee and Immigrant Assistance has reviewed the rule and wants to provide more information about the changing policies.

Public charge is a test that the federal government uses to determine whether certain people seeking to enter the United States or become a lawful permanent resident are likely to primarily depend on the government as a main source of support. If the government decides that someone is likely to be a public charge, they can be denied admission, a visa or lawful permanent residence status.

Here is what you need to know:

Public charge doesn't apply to all immigrants.

The rule might impact those applying for lawful permanent residency or admission to the United States — including diversity visa immigrants and applications to renew, change or extend visas in the United States.

Receipt of benefits doesn't mean someone is automatically going to be deemed a public charge. It is just one of the factors that an immigration officer may consider in the determination.

The new rule doesn't name any specific public benefit program but generally includes any means-tested public benefit program, including cash, food, medical and housing assistance.

Public charge doesn't impact everyone the same way. Every family is different and people should make decisions based on their specific situation.

People with questions or concerns about the impact of using public benefits on their immigration status should consider contacting an immigration lawyer. DSHS can't offer legal advice.

You can find more information on the DSHS public charge webpage.

https://t.co/MZQNfgwaPl

☆ Changes to Apple Health

Oct. 1, 2026, marked the first effective date for major Apple Health (Medicaid) eligibility changes directed by the federal House Resolution 1, or H.R. 1. These changes narrow eligibility for many lawfully present noncitizens, with about 11,000 Washington residents projected to lose coverage.

A new court order protects Apple Health coverage for more than 800 Washingtonians. You can learn more about this preliminary injunction and its impact on the Health Care Authority website.

DEA to Host 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24th, 2026.

Press Release
DEA to Host 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24th
WASHINGTON, DC –The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, in collaboration with more than 4,300 law enforcement partners, will host the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
More than 4,400 collection sites will be set up across the country to dispose of unneeded, expired, and unused prescription medications. This is a simple step that prevents diversion, reduces the risk of accidental poisonings, and helps protect communities.
“Since 2010, Take Back Day has helped Americans remove more than twenty million pounds of unneeded medications from their homes,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “By participating in Take Back Day, you are preventing potentially addictive medications from falling into the wrong hands – a small step that can save lives. I am grateful to the thousands of law enforcement and community partners who make these events possible, and I urge everyone to take a few minutes on Saturday, October 24, to clean out your medicine cabinets.”
What will be collected 
•Tablets, capsules, patches, and other forms of prescription medications
•Liquid medications securely sealed in their original containers
What won’t be collected
•Syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs
Why it matters
•Prescription opioids, such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, and morphine, are among the most frequently misused prescription pain medications, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA).
•Removing unneeded medications from the home reduces the risk of misuse or accidental ingestion.
Visit https://t.co/1D28VbGW3D to find a registered Take Back location near you. If you are unable to participate in this fall’s National Prescription Drug Take Back Day, there are more than 15,300 pharmacies, hospitals, and businesses that offer safe medication disposal year-round. In addition, many police departments also provide permanent drop boxes to ensure Every Day is Take Back Day.

text:
🏛️ Pittsboro Board of Commissioners 10.12.26 Meeting Summary

🏗️ Chatham Park South Village Development

- 🏘️ **Major residential development proposed:** Chatham Park and Southern Land Company presented plans for approximately 1,400–1,450 homes in South Village, significantly below the roughly 3,500 units permitted under existing zoning.

- 🏬 **Mixed-use commercial center:** The development includes plans for up to 325,000 square feet of nonresidential space, creating opportunities for shopping, services and other commercial activities.

- ⛳ **Private golf course, public neighborhood:** Southern Land Company confirmed the residential community will not be gated, although the golf club will remain private. Developers emphasized walkability, neighborhood connections and recreational amenities.

- 🏠 **Eleven housing types:** Developers plan to incorporate 11 different residential housing types throughout the community to provide variety in neighborhood design.

- 💰 **Developer promises financial commitment:** Southern Land Company founder and CEO Tim Downey pledged to personally support the project's financing, saying the company would not need bank loans or outside investment funds to complete its commitments.

- 🌳 **Environmental protection measures:** Plans include a 300-foot buffer along much of Roberson Creek, protection of approximately 31,000 linear feet of streams, and efforts to minimize grading, tree removal and water pollution.

- 🌿 **Golf course environmental certification:** Developers intend to pursue Audubon Cooperative Sanctuary Program certification and employ an environmental specialist throughout design and construction.

- 🚶 **Greenway relocation remains unresolved:** Approximately 1.8 miles of proposed greenway would be relocated because its original alignment conflicts with the golf course. The final route has not been determined.

- 🚒 **Public facilities:** Plans incorporate a potential fire station location and a roughly 50-acre public park. Chatham County Schools indicated it does not require a school site within the proposed development area.

- 🏡 **Affordable housing obligations:** Chatham Park's 7.5% affordable housing requirement would generate an estimated 95 affordable apartments and 11 affordable single-family units associated with this development. Most would be provided elsewhere within Chatham Park.

- 📅 **Decision expected in November:** Commissioners discussed the section design plans but did not approve them. A two-week public comment period was scheduled to begin October 13, with a potential vote in November.

 🚗 Transportation, Roads and Infrastructure

- 🛣️ **Chatham Parkway construction ahead of schedule:** Developers reported that the roadway connecting U.S. 64 Business and U.S. 15-501 was expected to be completed in approximately seven to eight months.

- 🚦 **Future traffic congestion raises concerns:** Transportation modeling identified potential capacity problems on East Street, Chatham Parkway, Moncure-Pittsboro Road and other major corridors as development continues.

- 📊 **Traffic studies requested:** Commissioners questioned whether traffic impact analyses should be completed before South Village receives approval rather than waiting until preliminary subdivision plans are submitted.

- ⚠️ **Unfunded roads complicate traffic projections:** Commissioners learned that some transportation models assume the construction of roads that currently lack funding. They requested updated analysis excluding those projects.

- 💵 **Road improvement costs remain uncertain:** Town staff said responsibility for funding future transportation improvements, including cost-sharing arrangements, has not yet been established.

- 🚑 **Emergency response concerns:** Commissioners questioned whether future congestion could affect fire and emergency response times, particularly as development expands.

- 🚧 **Western bypass access:** Commissioners discussed the need for additional access from the U.S. 64 bypass to serve future development southwest of downtown Pittsboro.

- 🚰 **Major sewer construction:** A 36-inch sewer force main along U.S. 15-501 is under construction, with completion anticipated in the third quarter of 2027.

- 💧 **Additional water infrastructure:** A 12-inch water line is being installed along Chatham Parkway, while another 36-inch line along Moncure-Pittsboro Road is expected to begin construction in the second quarter of 2027.

- 💲 **Long-term financial impact under review:** Developers and town staff are preparing a fiscal impact analysis that includes future infrastructure maintenance costs and the establishment of financial reserves.

 🏠 Roberts Run Affordable Housing Development

- ✅ **72-townhome subdivision approved:** Commissioners approved the preliminary plat for Roberts Run, a Chatham Habitat for Humanity development near Robert Street and I.E. Taylor Road.

- 📍 **Project location:** The approximately 25.91-acre property is located south of East Street and north of Roberson Creek.

- 🏘️ **Residential density:** The development proposes 72 townhomes at approximately 2.8 dwelling units per acre.

- 🌲 **Open space and greenways:** Plans include approximately 7.29 acres of open space, additional greenway easements, pedestrian paths and sidewalks.

- 🚶 **Pedestrian connections:** The subdivision will feature a 10-foot multiuse path, internal sidewalks and connections toward the Roberson Creek greenway network.

- 📆 **More than a decade in development:** Habitat representatives said the organization purchased the property in 2015 and expressed enthusiasm about reaching the preliminary approval stage.

- 🏗️ **Construction timeline:** Groundbreaking has not been scheduled. Construction drawings and additional approvals must be completed first.

- 👏 **Strong commissioner support:** Board members praised Habitat's efforts to provide compact, attainable housing in downtown Pittsboro.

### 🚌 Pittsboro Transportation on Demand

- 🚐 **New transportation service launched:** The mayor announced that Pittsboro Transportation on Demand, known as Pittsboro TOD, is operational.

- 💵 **$5 rides:** Residents can request transportation through an app, with pickup and transportation to another destination for a reported $5 fare.

- 📱 **Additional information forthcoming:** The town plans to provide more details about operating hours, app instructions and service availability.

- 🔄 **Change from original trolley concept:** The transportation program evolved from a proposed trolley system into an on-demand microtransit service.

### 🗺️ New Interactive Development Map

- 💻 **Public development-tracking tool introduced:** Town staff demonstrated an interactive online map designed to help residents follow development proposals and projects throughout Pittsboro.

- 🏗️ **Project information available:** Users can select developments to view locations, descriptions, parcel information and project status.

- 📍 **Town boundaries identified:** The map distinguishes Pittsboro's municipal limits from its extraterritorial jurisdiction.

- 🔎 **Additional features planned:** Staff are developing a major subdivision layer and hope to incorporate site plans, infrastructure projects and greenway information.

- 💬 **Residents can submit feedback:** An online form allows users to ask questions, recommend improvements and communicate with development services staff.

- 🔗 **County development information linked:** The town's website also provides access to Chatham County's development map.

 🏛️ Board Appointments and Planning Committees

- 🤝 **Affordable housing liaison:** Commissioner Foley was appointed the town's representative to the Chatham County Affordable Housing Advisory Committee.

- 🌳 **Parks and recreation liaison:** Commissioner Huninger was appointed as the Board of Commissioners' liaison to Pittsboro's Parks and Recreation Advisory Board.

- 📈 **Economic development steering committee approved:** Commissioners appointed members to a committee supporting the town's strategic economic development plan, covering healthcare, education, entrepreneurship, downtown development and other economic priorities.

- 🏙️ **Downtown master plan committee approved:** Commissioners approved an amended steering committee roster, adding engineering expertise and a student representative while adjusting membership.

- 👷 **Civil engineer added:** Landon Lovelace, president of Underfoot Engineering, requested and received support for joining the downtown master plan steering committee. He cited his experience with infrastructure, stormwater, roads and development.

- 🎓 **Youth representation:** Student representative London Crowley was added to the downtown master plan committee.

- 🗓️ **Temporary advisory committee:** Town staff indicated the downtown master plan steering committee is expected to meet approximately three or four times before completing its assignment.

 🗣️ Public Comments

- 🅿️ **Downtown parking concerns:** Longtime resident Vicky Old urged commissioners to develop additional downtown parking, particularly to accommodate older residents and support local businesses.

- 🚶 **Accessibility and downtown vitality:** Old emphasized the importance of safe, convenient access to downtown as Pittsboro grows.

- 🏗️ **Engineering perspective requested:** Landon Lovelace advocated including a licensed civil engineer on the downtown master plan committee to help evaluate infrastructure capacity, costs and project feasibility.

### 🌎 Environmental and Community Updates

- ⚡ **New electric vehicle charging station:** A commissioner reported that an eight-port DC fast-charging station had been installed at a Refuel location along U.S. 15-501 north of Pittsboro. It was not yet operational at the time of the meeting.

- 🌡️ **County climate planning:** The Chatham County Climate Advisory Committee continues reviewing potential data center standards and working with consultants on the county's Climate Action Plan.

- 🍂 **Leave the Leaves campaign:** Commissioners praised the town's public education campaign promoting environmentally beneficial yard practices.

- 🚲 **Bicycle safety outreach:** Pittsboro Police Department received praise for a bicycle safety video encouraging children to wear helmets.

- 🛠️ **Google Fiber issues addressed:** Commissioners thanked town staff for responding quickly to residents' concerns involving Google Fiber work.

- 🙏 **Public apology:** Commissioner Bonds apologized to Parks Director Katie Keller for comments made during previous meetings, acknowledging that his language should have been more respectful.

 💼 Business and Economic Development

- 💰 **Small business grants announced:** The Chatham Chamber of Commerce will begin accepting applications October 15 for 10 grants of $2,500 each, funded by the Duke Energy Foundation.

- 🏪 **Grant eligibility:** Established businesses may apply regardless of chamber membership. Funding is intended to help businesses modernize operations and pursue new opportunities.

- 📊 **Pittsboro ABC Board reports positive results:** A commissioner reported a clean annual audit and continued sales growth, noting the town's expansion and second ABC store.

- 🌾 **Leadership Chatham:** The program is celebrating its 21st year with 21 participants, including recent visits to local farms and the Pittsboro Farmers Market.

- 🎃 **Downtown Halloween decorations:** Commissioners praised downtown organizations and town staff for seasonal decorations and improvements.

### 🎉 Recognitions and Upcoming Events

- 🧘 **Pittsboro Yoga ribbon cutting:** The mayor attended the September 18 opening celebration at The Plant.

- 📚 **Dolly Parton Day:** Pittsboro celebrated its first Dolly Parton Day on September 25 with a library reading event in partnership with the Chatham Education Foundation.

- 🎖️ **World War II veteran honored:** The mayor proclaimed October 9 as Dr. George Chaw Day in recognition of the Pittsboro resident's 104th birthday and military service.

- 🎡 **Chatham County Fair:** The mayor highlighted strong community participation and attendance at the annual fair.

- 🏡 **Habitat for Humanity gala:** Commissioners attended Habitat's inaugural gala, praising community participation and efforts to expand affordable housing.

- 🗳️ **Election integrity statement:** Commissioner Foley called for respect for election workers, lawful vote counting and certified election results, while expressing concern about potential interference by outside authorities.

- 📅 **Legislative forum scheduled:** A state legislative forum featuring Sen. Natalie Murdock and Rep. Robert Reives was announced for December 17, from 4 to 7 p.m., followed by a local government appreciation reception.

 📌 Key Takeaways

- 🏗️ **Chatham Park South Village was the meeting's most consequential discussion**, with commissioners examining housing density, environmental protections, traffic congestion and long-term infrastructure costs.

- 🏠 **Roberts Run received preliminary plat approval**, advancing a 72-townhome Habitat for Humanity project near downtown.

- 🚗 **Transportation planning remains a major unresolved issue**, particularly how future road improvements will be funded and when traffic mitigation must occur.

- 🗺️ **The interactive development map offers residents a new way to monitor growth**, with additional information expected as the system develops.

- 🚌 **Pittsboro's $5 on-demand transportation service is operational**, marking a milestone in the town's local mobility efforts.

- 📆 **November will be important for South Village**, as commissioners are expected to revisit the section design plans after receiving public comments and additional information.

text:
October 13 Saint Edward the Confessor, King of England: From The Liturgical Year by Dom Prosper Louis Paschal Guéranger, O.S.B.
.
White Semidouble.
.
This glorious saint was like a beautiful lily, crowning the ancient branch of the kings of Wessex. The times had progressed since that sixth century, when the pagan Cerdic and other pirate chiefs from the North Sea scattered with ruins the island of saints. Having accomplished their mission of wrath, the Anglo-Saxons became instruments of grace to the land they had conquered. Evangelized by Rome, even as the Britons they had just chastized, they remembered, better than the latter, whence their salvation had come; a spring-tide blossoming of sanctity showed the pleasure God took once more in Albion, for the constant fidelity of the princes and people of the heptarchy towards the See of Peter. In the year of our Lord 800, Egbert, a descendant of Cerdic, had gone on pilgrimage to Rome, when a deputation from the West Saxons offered him the crown, beside the tomb of the Prince of the apostles, at whose feet Charlemagne, at that very time, was restoring the empire. As Egbert united under one scepter the power of the seven kingdoms, so Saint Edward, his last descendant, represents today in his own person the glorious holiness of them all.
.
Nephew to St. Edward the martyr, our holy king is known to God and man by the beautiful title of the Confessor. The Church, in her account of his life, sets forth more particularly the virtues which won him so glorious an appellation; but we must remember moreover that his reign of twenty-four years was one of the happiest England has ever known. Alfred the Great had no more illustrious imitator. The Danes, so long masters, now entirely subjugated within the kingdom, and without, held at bay by the noble attitude of the prince; Macbeth, the usurper of the Scotch throne, vanquished in a campaign that Shakespeare has immortalized; St. Edward’s Laws, which remain to this day the basis of the British constitution; the saint’s munificence towards all noble enterprises, while at the same time he diminished the taxes: all this proves with sufficient clearness, that the sweetness of virtue, which made him the intimate friend of St. John the beloved disciple, is not incompatible with the greatness of a monarch.
.
Eduardus, cognomento Confessor, nepos sancti Eduardi regis et martyris, Anglo-Saxonum regum ultimus, quem futurum regem Brithualdo viro sanctissimo in mentis excessu Dominus demonstravit, decennis a Danis Angliam vastantibus quæsitus ad necem: exsulare cogitur apud avunculum, Normanniæ ducem: ubi in mediis vitiorum illecebris talem se exhibuit integritate vitæ, morumque innocentia, ut omnibus admirationi esset. Eluxit in eo vel tum mira pietas in Deum ac res divinas, fuitque ingenio mitissimo, atque ab omni dominandi cupiditate alieno. Cujus ea vox fertur, malle se regno carere, quod sine cæde et sanguine obtineri non possit.
.
Edward, surnamed the Confessor, nephew to St. Edward king and martyr, was the last king of the Anglo-Saxon race. Our Lord had revealed that he would one day be king, to a holy man named Brithwald. When Edward was ten years old, the Danes, who were devastating England, sought his life; he was therefore obliged to go into exile, to the court of his uncle the duke of Normandy. Amid the vices and temptations of the Norman court, he grew up pure and innocent, a subject of admiration to all. His pious devotion towards God and holy things was most remarkable. He was of a very gentle disposition, and so great a stranger to ambition that he was wont to say he would rather forego the kingdom than take possession of it by violence and bloodshed.
.
Exstinctis mox tyrannis, qui fratribus suis vitam et regnum eripuerant, revocatur in patriam: ubi summis omnium votis et gratulatione regno potitus, ad hostilium irarum delenda vestigia totum se convertit, a sacris exorsus ac Divorum templis: quorum alia a fundamentis erexit, alia refecit, auxitque redditibus ac privilegiis; in eam curam potissimum intentus, ut refloresceret collapsa religio. Ab aulæ proceribus compulsum ad nuptias, constans est assertio scriptorum, cum virgine sponsa virginitatem in matrimonio servasse. Tantus in eo fuit in Christum amor et fides, ut illum aliquando inter Missarum solemnia videre meruerit blando vultu et divina luce fulgentem. Ob profusam caritatem, orphanorum et egenorum pater passim dicebatur, numquam lætior, quam cum regios thesauros exhausisset in pauperes.
.
On the death of the tyrants who had murdered his brothers and seized their kingdom, he was recalled to his country, and ascended the throne to the greatest satisfaction and joy of all his subjects. He then applied himself to remove all traces of the havoc wrought by the enemy. To begin at the sanctuary, he built many churches, and restored others, endowing them with rents and privileges; for he was very anxious to see religion, which had been neglected, flourishing again. All writers assert that, though compelled by his nobles to marry, both he and his bride preserved their virginity intact. Such were his love of Christ and his faith, that he was one day permitted to see our Lord in the Mass, shining with heavenly light and smiling upon him. His lavish charity won him the name of the father of orphans and of the poor; and he was never so happy as when he had exhausted the royal treasury on their behalf.
.
Prophetiæ dono illusstris, de Angliæ futuro statu multa cœlitus prævidit: et illus in primis memorabile quod Sweyni Danorum regis in mare demersi mortem, dum Angliam invadendi animo classem conscenderet, eodem quo accidit momento, divinitus intellexit. Joannem evangelistam mirifice coluit, nihil cuiquam, quod ejus nomine peteretur, negare solitus. Cui olim sub lacera veste suo nomine stipem roganti, cum nummi deessent, detractum ex digito annulum porrexit, quem Divus non ita multo post Eduardo remisit, una cum nuntio secuturæ mortis. Quare rex, indictis pro se precibus, ipso ab evangelista prædicto die, piissime obiit nonis videlicet Januarii, anno salutis millesimo sexagesimo sexto. Quem, sequenti sæculo, Alexander Papa tertius miraculis clarum sanctorum fastis adscripsit. At ejus memoriam Innocentius undecimus Officio publico per universam Ecclesiam eo die celebrari præcepit, quo annis ab obitu sex et triginta translatum ejus corpus incorruptum, et suavem spirans odorem, repertum est.
.
He was honored with the gift of prophecy, and foresaw much of England’s future history. A remarkable instance is, that when Sweyn, king of Denmark, was drowned in the very act of embarking on his fleet to invade England, Edward was supernaturally aware of the event the very moment it happened. He had a special devotion to St. John the evangelist, and was accustomed never to refuse anything asked in his name. One day St. John appeared to him as a poor man begging an alms in this manner; the king, having no money about him, took off his ring and gave it to him. Soon afterwards the saint sent the ring back to Edward, with a message that his death was at hand. The king then ordered prayers to be said for himself; and died most piously on the day foretold by St. John, the Nones of January, in the year of salvation 1066. In the following century Pope Alexander III enrolled him, famous for miracles, among the saints. Innocent XI ordered his memory to be celebrated by the whole Church with a public Office, on the day of his Translation, which took place thirty-six years after his death, his body being found incorrupt and exhaling a sweet fragrance.
.
Thou representest on the sacred cycle the nation which Gregory the Great foresaw would rival the angels; so many holy kings, illustrious virgins, grand bishops, and great monks, who were its glory, now form thy brilliant court. Where are now the unwise in whose sight thou and thy race seemed to die? History must be judged in the light of heaven. While thou and thine reign there eternally, judging nations and ruling over peoples; the dynasties of thy successors on earth, ever jealous of the Church, and long wandering in schism and heresy, have become extinct one after another, sterilized by God’s wrath, and having none but that vain renown whereof no trace is found in the book of life. How much more noble and more durable, O Edward, were the fruits of thy holy virginity! Teach us to look upon the present world as a preparation for another, an everlasting world; and to value human events by their eternal results. Our admiring worship seeks and finds thee in thy royal abbey of Westminster; and we love to contemplate, by anticipation, thy glorious resurrection on the day of judgment, when all around thee so many false grandeurs will acknowledge their shame and their nothingness. Bless us, prostrate in spirit or in reality beside thy tomb, where heresy, fearful of the result, would fain forbid our prayer. Offer to God the supplications rising today from all parts of the world, for the wandering sheep, whom the Shepherd’s voice is now so earnestly calling back to the one fold!

text:
Brother Sisay,

This is the exchange working as it should. Let me answer it the same way you have — by conceding what you have carried before pressing what I think you have not.

ON THE STANDARD, YOU ARE RIGHT, AND I WITHDRAW THE POINT.

The distinction between a public framework and confidential negotiating detail is real, and I should have drawn it myself. Nobody is owed phone records. Goals, limits, mutual commitments, decision-making, safeguards and exit conditions are a different matter, and asking for them is legitimate.

But see what your own distinction now asks of you. You named six things a framework should make public. Your roadmap offers four: independent Amhara political agency, a clear mandate, protection of core Amhara concerns, and partnerships built on shared interests.

Those are commitments about posture, not about structure. They do not say who decides, what the limits are, which safeguards exist, or how one exits. By the standard you have just articulated — which I accept — your roadmap is thinner today than the framework you are criticising. That is fixable in a paragraph, and I would genuinely like to read it.

ON DISPERSAL, YOU ARE PARTLY RIGHT TOO.

Three fronts do not produce equal relief, and anyone who claims otherwise is selling something. The regime has never distributed its violence evenly, and Amhara has borne the worst of the air campaign while other fronts were active. I accept that.

But the comparison is the wrong one. The question is not whether Amhara suffered while three fronts burned. It is whether Amhara suffers more or less when it stands closest to alone. We have run that experiment as well.

Pretoria closed the largest front in the country in November 2022. Within five months the government moved to dissolve the Amhara regional forces. By August 2023 it had placed the region under a state of emergency. In the first year of that emergency alone, AAA counted 53 drone attacks that killed people. Merawi came that January. By April 2025 ACLED had recorded 73 air and drone strikes, and Gedeb killed more than a hundred in one strike.

The heaviest concentration of state violence against Amhara in living memory began in the months after the state's largest adversary stopped fighting. That is not coincidence. It is capacity. When the north went quiet, the drones did not stand down. They moved.

And notice where your own observation leads. If the regime singles out Amhara regardless of what else is burning, then quieting the other fronts does not spare us — it releases the capacity that was tied up elsewhere. Your evidence establishes the regime's intent toward Amhara more than it refutes dispersal.

ON WHAT A SEAT CAN ACTUALLY SHAPE — THIS IS YOUR BEST QUESTION.

"What decisions can that seat shape? Whose priorities does it protect? What recourse is there if commitments are ignored?" That is exactly right, and it should be asked loudly and often.

It also has an answer now that it did not have a month ago.

On 17 September the OLA publicly demanded that Fano dissociate itself from the Fano command in Wollega, calling it regime-backed. That was the first real test of whether Amhara interests would be traded away to keep the coalition intact. AFNM refused. It affirmed that the Bizamo Command falls under its own command, and the Wollega formations — protecting the most exposed Amhara communities in the country — stayed inside the movement rather than being cut loose to buy goodwill.

That is a decision the seat shaped, within weeks of the founding, in favour of the communities with the least protection and the smallest voice. It is one data point and I will not inflate it into a guarantee. But it is a data point, which is more than any roadmap has.

As for recourse: that is what published benchmarks and a no-separate-peace commitment are for. Recourse among armed movements is never a court. It is the cost of visible defection, and that cost exists only if the terms were stated in advance, in p-

At the time of the writing of...
The US Constitution  and the 2nd Amendment...

Our forefathers were envisioning the individual owing of the the latest technology in weapons....  That has not changed other than the "latest technology"...

Advanced Firearms of the Late 18th Century

Girandoni Air Rifle (1779): 
A repeating air rifle featuring a tubular magazine holding around 22 balls, capable of firing up to 60 rounds per minute with an effective range of about 150 yards. It was even issued in military service, including by the Austrian army. 

Ferguson Rifle (1774): 
A breakthrough breech-loading flintlock rifle used in limited numbers during the American Revolutionary War. It allowed a soldier to load and fire much faster than standard muzzleloaders and offered high accuracy due to tight rifling.

Belton Repeating Flintlock (1777): 
Developed by Joseph Belton, this "rapid-fire" repeating flintlock could hold and discharge multiple rounds (ranging from 8 to 20 shots) in rapid succession.
